# hands/firsts

the firsts calendar, posted only when bin/proofs confirms.

## How to call it

Run it from the repository root with your shell (exec) tool: `hands/firsts <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

- Acting (side effects in the world, each goes through the guard and the caps): announce
- Job (writes state or calls the core): none
- Operator only (never call): none
- Read only: list; due

## Verbs

| Verb | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | R | Every first in the calendar with its proof's `status`, `has` and `need` from `bin/proofs`, and `announced` once it was posted. |
| `due` | R | `{firsts, rounds}`: the firsts whose proof is `met` and never announced, and the round numbers (100, 250, 500, 1000, 2500, ...) that `x.followers`, `moltbook.karma`, `github.stars` or `github.followers` crossed in the last 7 days of `stats` and never announced (the highest per m… |
| `announce` | A | `{text, first}` or `{text, round}`. |

Kinds: R = read: no side effect beyond its read cache; A = acting: posts, sends, pays or opens something in the world; O = operator-only: the operator runs it, never you; J = job: writes state or calls the core, says nothing to anyone; scheduled jobs run it, you do not.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `announce`, `due`, `list`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `hands/firsts <verb> --help` (never put a VAR= in front of a command: the shell refuses it, and DRY_RUN is not yours to set). The full account is in docs/hands.md.
